reports.title: AMGEN REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 FINANCIAL RESULTS

guidance.heading: 2026 Guidance
section: For the full year 2026, the Company expects:
•Total revenues in the range of $38.9 billion to $39.7 billion.
•On a GAAP basis, EPS in the range of $18.34 to $19.28, and a tax rate in the range of 14.5% to 16.0%.
•On a non-GAAP basis, EPS in the range of $22.90 to $23.70, and a tax rate in the range of 15.0% to 16.5%.

desk.headline: Revenue up 8% to $10.4bn and adjusted EPS $6.45, both beat; 2026 outlook now $38.9–39.7bn revenue
results: Total revenue rose 8% to $10.37bn; product sales grew 8%, mainly on higher volumes. Seventeen products grew at least 10%.
Growth came from Repatha (+37%), EVENITY (+39%), TEZSPIRE (+43%), UPLIZNA (+191%) and cancer drug IMDELLTRA (+128%).
Bone drugs Prolia (-45%) and XGEVA (-47%) fell sharply as cheaper biosimilar copies launched; Otezla fell 18%.
GAAP EPS rose 19% to $7.08 and adjusted EPS 14% to $6.45. Free cash flow dipped to $3.65bn from $4.25bn on working-capital timing.
Dividend of $2.52 a share (up 6%); no shares bought back in the quarter. Cash $13.2bn, debt $54.0bn.

guidance.summary: For 2026 Amgen expects revenue of $38.9–39.7bn and adjusted EPS of $22.90–23.70. The release gives no earlier range, but call coverage described this as a raise; a pre-results preview put the previous range at $38.2–39.4bn and $22.30–23.50.

points: Management stressed that Repatha's growth is speeding up, with US new-patient prescriptions up more than 60%.
Six key growth products rose 27% and now make up over 70% of product sales, offsetting biosimilar losses on Prolia and XGEVA.
Weight-loss drug MariTide is in late-stage trials, and three studies have finished enrolling; no launch date was given.
The finance chief said he does not expect operating margin to step down in 2027 compared with 2026.
Strong survival data for lung-cancer drug IMDELLTRA was described as an important advance for patients.
